poiCHI-desc:
For more than a century China was the hegemon of the East, rising as its rivals were weakened by decades of social, political and economic upheaval. When the Great Mistake came, the Chinese People's Party was the one government on Earth that had seen it coming. It had prepared its cities, its granaries and its coastlines long before the first warning, and for a time that foresight made China the sole world leader, taking the place the old United States had left empty.

The victory did not last. Decades of floods and environmental disasters have left Beijing barely able to hold its own country together, let alone a sphere of influence that shrinks every year. Recovery came at a price: vast inequality, automation that has made millions redundant, and corruption that reaches into every ministry. The result is a disenfranchised population that is growing more radical with each passing season.

The Cooperative is the successor to China's old sphere. Its members include Korea, Japan, the mainland states of Southeast Asia and the provinces of the Chinese People's Republic itself, tied together by trade, shared defence and the memory of a stronger Beijing. Its provinces, from Guangdong and the Yangtze to Sichuan, Dongbei and the Beijing region, are some of the richest and most industrial places on Earth, and some of the most restless.

The world's centre cannot hold.
CHIpoi001-desc: China has been ruled by a single party since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949. Many reforms have come and gone since then, but in many ways the Chinese government is a relic of the world before the Great Mistake, poorly adapted to face the crisis now at its door.
CHIpoi002-desc: After the Great Mistake, China emerged as the sole world leader, replacing the old United States. Decades of floods and other environmental disasters have since left it barely able to maintain control over its own territory, let alone a sphere of influence that keeps shrinking.
CHIpoi003-desc: The death of Party Chairwoman Fu Zhong last year under suspicious circumstances has inflamed an already delicate political situation. National leadership is being contested between several factions of the People's Party, which degrades its already low legitimacy even further. Political groups outside the Party continue to grow in power, and the country becomes more decentralised by the year.
CHIpoi004-desc: China faces many challenges, but it remains the undisputed world leader in many industrial sectors. Its large, well-educated population is unmatched by any other nation.
CHIpoi005-desc: The Strategic Cooperation Organisation was formed in the golden age of Chinese international power, mainly as a means for Beijing to trade with its sphere and influence it. Decades of flooding have left that influence far weaker, and the organisation has taken on a more balanced role as an economic and military alliance. With political turmoil in many of its member states, the SCO may soon be relegated to the history books.
CHIpoi006-desc: Last year Fu Zhong, China's de jure leader and the figurehead of the federal clique, died of a stroke at the relatively young age of 62. Her death has become the focus of many conspiracy theories, since it came in the middle of a succession dispute between the federal clique and the unitary clique led by Liang Xiaowen. Sun Zongying has since taken her place as leader of the federal clique, and the crisis shows no sign of ending.
